content: 1. Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of bearberry by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 2. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of benazepril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of benzphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of betaxolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and reduces its levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 5. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Bictegravir can be taken under fasting conditions 2 hours before antacids containing calcium. However, bictegravir and calcium-containing supplements can be taken together with food. Routine administration of bictegravir (under fasting conditions) simultaneously with, or 2 hours after, calcium supplements or antacids containing calcium is not recommended. 6. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of bisoprolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and reduces its levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 7. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of bosutinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Bosutinib exhibits pH-dependent solubility; short-acting antacids may be used with administration separated by 2 hours. 8. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent. Co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may cause premature dissolution of these budesonide products, potentially affecting release properties and drug absorption in the duodenum. 9. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of cabotegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Calcium carbonate also decreases the levels or effects of cabotegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Administer antacid products at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after taking oral cabotegravir. 10. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of captopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism and may reduce its absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 12. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Calcium carbonate also decreases the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of carvedilol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and reduces its levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 14. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Calcium carbonate also decreases the levels or effects of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. 15. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Calcium carbonate also decreases the levels or effects of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Calcium carbonate also decreases the levels or effects of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Calcium carbonate also decreases the levels or effects of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of celecoxib by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 19. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of ciprofloxacin with multivalent cation-containing products may reduce ciprofloxacin bioavailability by up to 90%. Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after using these products. Use alternatives if available. 20. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may decrease the solubility of crizotinib and subsequently reduce its bioavailability. However, no formal studies have been conducted. 21. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of celiprolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and reduces its levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 22. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of deferiprone by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Deferiprone may bind polyvalent cations (e.g., iron, aluminum, and zinc). Separate administration by at least 4 hours between deferiprone and other medications (e.g., antacids) or supplements containing these polyvalent cations. 23. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of chenodiol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 24. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by cation binding in the GI tract. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 25. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium salts. 26. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of clevidipine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of cyclosporine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Famotidine increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Delayed resorption of cyclosporine has been reported when famotidine is co-administered with cyclosporine. 28. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that alter upper GI tract pH (e.g., PPIs, H2-blockers, antacids) may decrease dabrafenib solubility and reduce its bioavailability. Calcium carbonate also decreases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. 29. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of deferiprone by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Deferiprone may bind polyvalent cations (e.g., iron, aluminum, and zinc). Separate administration by at least 4 hours between deferiprone and other medications (e.g., antacids) or supplements containing these polyvalent cations. 30. Magnesium hydroxide and deflazacort both decrease serum potassium. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Famotidine increases the levels or effects of dexmethylphenidate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. This applies only to extended-release formulations. 32. Deferoxamine decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Deferoxamine chelates iron; its affinity for other minerals is unknown. 33. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Oral delafloxacin forms chelates with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. 34. Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Calcium carbonate increases the effects of digoxin by pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of diltiazem by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Use caution and monitor closely. Administer dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking medications containing polyvalent cations; use alternative therapy if available. Calcium carbonate also decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Administer dolutegravir 2 hours (dolutegravir or abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine) or 4 hours (dolutegravir/rilpivirine) before or 6 hours after taking medications containing polyvalent cations. 38. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Elvitegravir plasma concentrations are lower with antacids due to the formation of ionic complexes in the GI tract and not due to changes in gastric pH; separate dose from antacid by at least 2 hours. 39. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of fleroxacin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 40. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration from antacids by 2 hours. 41. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of enalapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of ephedrine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Famotidine increases the levels of erdafitinib by decreasing renal clearance. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider alternatives that are not OCT2 substrates or consider reducing the dose of OCT2 substrates based on tolerability. 44. Famotidine decreases the levels of erlotinib by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid combination when possible. If concurrent use is required, erlotinib should be taken 10 hours after an H2-antagonist and at least 2 hours before the next dose of the H2-antagonist. 45. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of erythromycin base by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of esmolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and reduces its levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 50. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of estramustine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients should take estramustine with water at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. 51. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of etidronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 30 minutes. 52. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of felodipine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of ferric maltol by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Famotidine also decreases the levels or effects of ferric maltol by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Famotidine also decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of ferrous gluconate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Calcium carbonate also decreases the levels or effects of ferrous gluconate by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of flecainide by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Calcium carbonate also decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of fosinopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Famotidine decreases the levels of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate gefitinib and H2-antagonist doses by at least 6 hours. 61. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of gabapentin by inhibiting GI absorption.
